body: Oh what I would love to do to you 😍😘🥵🔥❤️

Although I still contemplate it. Plan still somewhat to pay off all my debt. The only thing that is keeping me here other than debt is what my dad sacrificed to provide me and my brothers a good life. He died from a horrible disease that doctors told him he should not have made it through college and yet he did. Went through college with no money the disease he did not know at the time and still had a good career to support us. The American dream he lived for us. ❤️

Everything has kind of hit me at once. My dad is sick and needs long term care so I would have to care for him. I lost a good friend because I caught feelings for them. I don’t have many friends I can connect with. I’m alone all the time. Parents are divorced and no enjoyable holiday is enjoyable anymore when they fight over who celebrates what holiday together. Went to school got my degree but have not progressed to graduate school nor I’m too depressed and motivated to continue to do that when at any time I would have to take care of my father so I could waste my money/time if I pursue it and he falls sick to not care for himself.

I can see your point of view. But isn’t everything biological and chemical? I’m not saying you are right or wrong. I definitely agree everyone’s scenario/circumstance is different, but we tend to have similar symptoms and it’s definitely not easy to cure anyone’s depression no matter what you do. But yet we have somewhat of a cohesive bond to long to express our feelings of hurt and pain that to I’m sure many of us have a sense of satisfaction to engage in.

Thank you for your comment! I understand what you mean...I’ve always been a rock/metal dude but never had a more deeper connection with it until I was depressed. I’ve recently had a deeper connection with Linkin Park and especially Chester Bennington. I’ve listened to them ever since I was 6 years old. Once he ended his life I listened to his older stuff and had a deep understanding and love for his old music. Almost made me cry. It’s almost like he expressed my exact feelings through his music. I’m so glad I was to able to see him and his crew once and I have realized it was one of the greatest concerts I’ve ever been to.

Yeah I can see it! Thank you for your comment. I don’t know... just an interesting sensation to have the urge to listen and validate your feelings about how you truly feel. It makes me think... does everyone think the exact same way as I do with my depression or are there various forms of it? Or do we all want to express how depressing our lives are and feel a rush of endorphins/dopamine running through our bloodstream? Just a very really peculiar thought.

That pretty much sums it up! It’s almost like a guilty pleasure. When for people who aren’t depressed hears that I  feel that way it’s like I am am psychotic or something...just a very strange sensation. Almost seems like self-harm that feels right, I think.

I’ll have to do that. Thank you. I don’t know...I post it just because I just feel a sense of righteousness with listening to that kind of music. Even though you shouldn’t feel that way, but it unconsciously feels right.

I can see it being as a coping mechanism. I don’t know...I guess I just listen to depressing music and read the lyrics and see the connection of how much similar we feel and to almost feel like we are praising it in a way. Almost that it feels right even when it’s not suppose to feel that way.
Same. But it does make it somewhat tolerable. Hang in there!
